newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-MARSEILLE DENT BASTIA'S TITLE HOPES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARSEILLE DENT BASTIA'S TITLE HOPES.

text.p: Marseille dented Bastia's title hopes with a 1-0 home win over the third-placed Corsicans, who were down to 10 men for the last 20 minutes, in the French first division on Saturday.

Bastia, who had won seven of their eight previous matches in their bid to keep pace with leaders Monaco and second-placed Paris St Germain, had left back Patrick Valery sent off in the 70th minute for a second bookable offence.
The defeat left Bastia still six points behind Monaco and two short of PSG, who clash in Monaco on Sunday.

Former France striker Xavier Gravelaine scored on the stroke of halftime to lift Marseille two places to ninth, chesting down a cross from the right from Ludovic Asuar and volleying past Bastia goalkeeper Laurent Weber.
Bastia's 12-goal Yugoslav striker Anto Drobnjak missed an easy equaliser when he headed wide after the interval.
"We're relieved (to have won), Bastia are not third for nothing," said Jean-Michel Roussier, chief executive of former European champions Marseille, who are desperate to qualify for Europe this year.
Most teams were slow warming to the task, scoring only five first half goals in eight games, following a month's winter recess.
Fourth-placed Bordeaux scored three times in the last five minutes, twice in injury time, as they beat bottom club Nice 4-1 at home.

Striker Pascal Nouma scored twice, his second goal a superb lob, as Strasbourg beat Rennes 3-0 to retain fifth place. It was the eighth consecutive away loss for Rennes, who have the worst away record in the division.
Midfielder Jocelyn Blanchard also hit two goals, his second an injury-time winner, as sixth-placed Metz beat relegation candidates Nancy 3-2 away.
Metz were two goals up inside an hour through France striker Robert Pires and Blanchard but Nancy fought back to pull level with two goals from defender Eric Rabesandratana in the last four minutes.

Nantes extended their unbeaten run in the league to 17 games with a 1-1 draw at home against Le Havre, conceding an equaliser by Nicolas Huysman less than a minute after going in front with a header by defender Jean-Marc Chanelet.
Coach Jean-Claude Suaudeau, referring to the performance of Le Havre's France reserve goalkeeper Christophe Revault, said: "Revault was exceptional. This evening one man alone kept us out."
But he said he was happy with his team who "recovered their confidence after losing in both (domestic) cups."
Le Havre scorer Huysman, whose side are 15th, said: "This point was not in our calculations (for survival in the top flight). These kind of points are the ones that may save us (from relegation)."
